results.controlIntent: a. Internal system clocks are used to generate time stamps for audit records; and b. Time stamps recorded for audit records meet [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] and use Coordinated Universal Time, have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time, or include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both CloudTrail audit records retrieved for the churn-predictor-endpoint use timestamps generated by AWS internal system clocks (satisfying AU-8.v2.a). The CreateEndpoint event (b5dfed62) records eventTime "2025-12-01T11:00:00Z" and the UpdateEndpoint event (a0837a00) records eventTime "2026-03-15T14:22:00Z". Both timestamps: (1) are in ISO 8601 format, (2) use Coordinated Universal Time explicitly denoted by the 'Z' suffix, and (3) carry second-level granularity (HH:MM:SS), which is substantively adequate for audit record purposes under SP 800-53 Rev 5. The use of UTC across all observed events is consistent and unambiguous. Confidence is medium rather than high because no organization-defined granularity policy document was available to confirm the required precision level matches the observed second-level granularity, and the evidence set covers only two events.
gaps: No organization-defined granularity policy document was available to confirm the required time measurement precision (e.g., millisecond vs. second) — human attestation or policy retrieval needed to fully validate AU-8.v2.b's assignment parameter.

Only two CloudTrail events were retrieved; a broader sample across more event types (e.g., model registry approvals, data access events) would increase confidence that UTC timestamping is applied consistently across all audit record sources.

No evidence of clock synchronization configuration (e.g., NTP/AWS Time Sync Service settings) was available to directly confirm AU-8.v2.a's requirement that internal system clocks are the authoritative source.
